anya: Heads up — since yesterday's kernel-routing tweaks I'm seeing a 15-25% increase in P99 latency on mixed-model tenants (2x small + 1x large). P50 looks fine. Flamegraph attached: https://perf-uploads/redwood/fg_1799998523.svg :thinking_face:

mateo: ugh. can you paste the profiler top funcs? kernel fallback maybe?

anya: pasted minimal trace:
```
# sample stackcounts
runtime::dispatch_kernel 45.6%
kv_cache::evict_scan 18.4%
allocator::compact_on_alloc 12.3%
cuda::memcpy_async 7.1%
other 16.6%
```

devin: that `kv_cache::evict_scan` number looks high. are we thrashing KV entries between models? what does `gpu_memstats` show for fragmented vs free?

anya: memstats (snip):
```
total_vram: 40GB
allocated: 31.2GB
free_contiguous: 600MB
fragmented_free: 1.8GB
slab_overhead: 1.0GB
kv_cached: 7.4GB
active_workspaces: 18
```

lila: FYI that allocator tuning (commit 9f8b7c) enabled aggressive slab-split for small allocs — we intentionally traded fragmentation for faster allocs. looks like on mixed-tenancy workloads that trade is hurting because of kernel fallback + repeated KV evictions.

devin: hypothesis: small-model churn causes repeated tiny frees that fragment slabs; then large-model requests hit kernel paths that need large contiguous workspaces -> kernel selection falls back to slower kernels and triggers more copies. two levers: (1) compact-on-alloc for requests that need contiguous regions, (2) prefer soft-slice isolation for small models so they don't fragment the shared slab.

anya: tried soft-slice pinning on one small model with `infractl v1 alloc --slice=soft --models=small-a`; result: P99 dropped ~9% but we got intermittent OOMs on the large model after spike.

infra-bot: NOTE: node gpu-08 restarted (OOM kill) at 2026-03-16T03:12:05Z — auto-recover initiated.

mateo: OOMs make sense — soft-slice lowered fragmentation but decreased headroom for transient large contiguous allocs. we need an adaptive policy: detect high fragmentation + active large-model load -> temporarily reserve a contiguous pool or trigger compact-on-demand with low-latency path.

devin: I can add two metrics for canary: `gpu.vram.fragmentation_ratio` and `kv.eviction_rate_by_model` and an alert if fragmentation_ratio > 0.25 and kv.eviction_rate rises > 3x baseline.

lila: +1. also propose a short canary: add compact-on-demand that runs async with priority for requests where `required_contiguous >= 1GB` and fragmentation_ratio > threshold. should only run on staging first. I'll open rollout PR.

anya: happy to run microbench on staging with synthetic mixed-tenancy trace (seq len mix, 2small+1large). I'll collect flamegraphs and memstats.

devin: I'll instrument kernel-selection to emit which kernel variant was chosen and why (reason codes: `fast_path`, `fallback_contig`, `fallback_copy`).

mateo: plan sounds good. if compact-on-demand reduces latency tails without causing OOMs, we can sequence-deploy. otherwise fallback to conservative slab-split.

lila: putting this on tomorrow's deploy window. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/alloc/pulls/1423 — reviewers @devin @anya. :thumbsup:

anya: thanks — will post results here after two runs.

mateo: thx — also add a short perf test that simulates kernel fallback (force `cuda_ctx.flags = fallback`) so we can measure worst-case regression before rollout.

anya: noted. starting run 1 now.
